verdictScope: Bounded report acceptance with explicit qualifications and coordinator dispositions; not wholesale adoption of every sentence or publication approval.

F1.decision: Accepted, low severity, as direct ice/freezing label precautions.
F1.basis: Daijisen explicitly defines 霜 as ice crystals and refrigerator frost as fine ice (05-extract:17-18). Actual labels are frost, ice; freeze and freeze; frozen; no endpoint declares either pair. KANJIDIC projection:28,109 independently retains frozen/refrigerate and ice/freeze. Existing 冷/寒 precautions make the narrower ice/freezing omission inconsistent.
F1.required: Add 氷 and 凍 to 霜's direct quiz_exclusions with a short qualified Notes explanation, preserving metadata, readings and geometry; validate and rebuild the manifest.
F1.qualification: Not synonymy: frost is deposited ice, not every freezing event. The cited English frost-heaving/permafrost discussion does not establish a new Japanese bare-霜 sense. Accept based on the ordinary ice/freezing label overlap, not that English extrapolation or a universal hypernym-exclusion rule.

F2.decision: Accepted, low severity, as a direct protective-aid precaution.
F2.basis: Actual 援 article:66-72 explicitly discusses help/save and protection/rescue, while 衛 displays guard; defense. Independent KANJIDIC projection:2,87 gives 衛 protection and 援 save; Daijisen 01-extract:12 gives 守る. Neither endpoint declares the pair.

F2.qualification: Not inferred merely from both cards excluding 守/防: those pairs are not transitive. Direct protect/save evidence supports the precaution; general assistance and all forms of aid are not defense.
